tests.name: MHPCO Claim Office quotes an empty item list as premium 5 G (processing fee only)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single plain sword (base 100 G) for a 0-year customer as premium 115 G (100 + 10 first insurance + 5 fee)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single plain amulet (base 60 G) for a 0-year customer as premium 71 G (60 + 6 first insurance + 5 fee)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single plain staff (base 80 G) for a 0-year customer as premium 93 G (80 + 8 first insurance + 5 fee)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a single plain potion (base 40 G) for a 0-year customer as premium 49 G (40 + 4 first insurance + 5 fee)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 1 rune (component base 25 G) for a 0-year customer as premium 33 G (25 + 2.5 first insurance + 5 fee, rounded up from 32.5)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 1 moonstone (component base 25 G) for a 0-year customer as premium 33 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 2 runes as base premium 50 G -> premium 60 G (no block)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 3 runes as base premium 60 G -> premium 71 G (block applies)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 4 runes as base premium 100 G -> premium 115 G (no block -- block requires exactly 3)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 7 runes as base premium 175 G -> premium 198 G (no block -- block requires exactly 3)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 2 runes + 1 moonstone as base premium 75 G -> premium 88 G (no block: alike means same type)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 3 runes + 3 moonstones as base premium 120 G -> premium 137 G (two separate blocks, one per type)
MHPCO Claim Office quotes 3 moonstones as base premium 60 G -> premium 71 G (block applies to moonstones too)
MHPCO Claim Office adds a 50 % curse surcharge to the cursed item's base premium: cursed sword -> premium 165 G
MHPCO Claim Office adds a 30 % high-enchantment surcharge for enchantment exactly 5: sword -> premium 145 G
MHPCO Claim Office adds no high-enchantment surcharge for enchantment 4: sword -> premium 115 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies both curse and high-enchantment surcharges to a cursed sword with enchantment exactly 5 -> premium 195 G

MHPCO Claim Office applies the curse surcharge only to the cursed item, not the policy total: cursed sword + plain amulet -> base 160 G, curse adds 50 G, first insurance 16 G, fee 5 G -> premium 231 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies the 20 % loyalty discount at exactly 2 years with MHPCO: plain sword -> premium 95 G (100 + 10 first insurance - 20 loyalty + 5 fee)
MHPCO Claim Office applies no loyalty discount at 1 year with MHPCO: plain sword -> premium 115 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies the 10 % first-insurance surcharge on the policy base premium of every quote: plain staff for a 0-year customer -> premium 93 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies a 15 % follow-up-contract discount to the customer's second quote in the scenario: plain sword -> premium 100 G (100 + 10 first insurance - 15 follow-up + 5 fee)
MHPCO Claim Office applies no follow-up-contract discount to the customer's first quote: plain sword -> premium 115 G
MHPCO Claim Office adds the 5 G processing fee at the very end of the premium calculation: empty policy -> 5 G, plain potion -> 49 G
MHPCO Claim Office rounds a premium of 197.5 G up to 198 G (rounding in the MHPCO's favour): 7 runes for a 0-year customer
MHPCO Claim Office keeps intermediate amounts as fractions and rounds only the final premium: 1 rune for a 2-year customer -> 22.5 + 5 = 27.5 -> premium 28 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a newcomer's cursed steel sword (enchantment 3, 0 years) as premium 165 G
MHPCO Claim Office quotes a 3-year customer's second contract for a cursed steel sword (enchantment 7) as premium 160 G
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a quote containing an item of unknown type (broomstick) by throwing an Error naming the unknown type
MHPCO Claim Office pays out 400 G for a regular steel sword (enchantment 3) with 500 G damage (full reimbursement minus 100 G deductible)
MHPCO Claim Office pays out 100 G for a damaged rune (insurance value 250 G) with 200 G damage (no enchantment or material, so no special clause)
MHPCO Claim Office applies the 100 G deductible once per damaged item: sword 500 G + amulet 300 G in one incident -> payout 600 G
MHPCO Claim Office reimburses damage to an item with enchantment >= 8 at 50 %: steel sword enchantment 9, damage 1000 G -> payout 400 G
MHPCO Claim Office fully reimburses damage to a dragon-material item: dragon sword enchantment 5, damage 800 G -> payout 700 G
MHPCO Claim Office lets the 50 % rule win when both clauses apply: dragon sword enchantment 9, damage 1000 G -> payout 400 G
MHPCO Claim Office applies the high-enchantment clause at exactly enchantment 8: dragon sword, damage 1000 G -> payout 400 G
MHPCO Claim Office caps the payout at twice the insurance sum: sword (sum 1000 G, cap 2000 G), first claim of 1500 G -> payout 1400 G, remainingCap 600 G
MHPCO Claim Office reduces a later claim to the remaining cap: second claim of 1500 G on the same sword policy -> payout 600 G, remainingCap 0 G
MHPCO Claim Office derives the insurance sum from all covered items: sword + amulet -> sum 1600 G, cap 3200 G
MHPCO Claim Office bases the cap on unmodified insurance values: cursed sword (premium 165 G with modifiers) -> cap 2000 G
MHPCO Claim Office excludes the block discount from the insurance sum: sword + 3 runes -> sum 1750 G, cap 3500 G
MHPCO Claim Office insures two swords as insurance sum 2000 G with cap 4000 G
MHPCO Claim Office treats each of two sword damage entries as a separate damage with its own deductible when two swords are insured: 500 G + 300 G -> payout 600 G
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a claim with more damage entries of a type than the policy covers (two sword damages, one sword insured) by throwing an Error
MHPCO Claim Office rounds a payout of 350.5 G down to 350 G (rounding in the MHPCO's favour): sword enchantment 9, damage 901 G -> 450.5 - 100 = 350.5 -> payout 350 G
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a claim referencing an item not part of the policy (amulet damaged, only a sword insured) by throwing an Error
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a claim referencing a damaged item of unknown type by throwing an Error
MHPCO Claim Office rejects a claim containing a damage entry with amount -200 by throwing an Error
MHPCO Claim Office reads a scenario from stdin and writes a results array of the same length and order to stdout
MHPCO Claim Office returns premium for quote results and payout plus remainingCap for claim results, as integers
MHPCO Claim Office resolves a claim's zero-based policy step index to the policy created by that earlier quote step
MHPCO Claim Office exits non-zero and writes an error description to stderr when a quote item has an unknown type
